article_title: VS Code 1.143 Makes the Copilot Harness the Default for New Sessions and Adds Model Comparison and Worktree Cleanup

content_preview.title: VS Code 1.143 Makes the Copilot Harness the Default for New Sessions and Adds Model Comparison and Worktree Cleanup
content_preview.summary: Visual Studio Code 1.143 makes the Copilot harness the default for new sessions, adds a preview of side-by-side model comparison and an experimental cleanup for inactive agent worktrees.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft released Visual Studio Code 1.143 on October 22, 2026, according to the [1.143.0 release tag on GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/releases/tag/1.143.0), which shows the tag published at 13:00 UTC. The [release notes](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_143) say the update "makes the Copilot harness the default for new sessions and adds tools to compare models, reclaim storage, run models locally, and navigate file changes." A follow-up build, 1.143.1, is lis...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (829 words by the script count, 820 excluding link URLs; range 400-1200). Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know and Context sections are clear and proportionate. Dense with specifics, all of which trace to the release notes.
editor_notes.source_verification: Two sources, both first-party Microsoft: code.visualstudio.com (VS Code release notes) and github.com/microsoft/vscode (release tag). Both hostnames are exact entries on config/source_allowlist.txt (github.com line 1131, code.visualstudio.com line 1190). Read from disk: source-0.html.gz (release notes, HTTP 200, sha256 in manifest, suspicious_patterns null) and source-1.html.gz (GitHub tag, HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null); then live re-fetched both via WebFetch and cross-checked against raw snapshot text. CONFIRMED against source-0: highlight sentence 'This release makes the Copilot harness the default for new sessions and adds tools to compare models, reclaim storage, run models locally, and navigate file changes.' verbatim; 'The Copilot harness is now the default for new sessions in VS Code. It's our latest harness, built on the Copilot SDK, a shared foundation that helps align behavior, capabilities, and improvements across Copilot products.' verbatim; background-running and editor/Agents window access, and 'run through the Agent Host', confirmed. The default-harness claim is scoped by the notes to 'new sessions in VS Code'; the notes state no opt-out in that section (the harness picker is shown, and the enterprise section describes Local as disabled/retired); the article does not claim an opt-out exists or not, and says nothing beyond the source. Compare models: setting sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled, Agents window only, labelled Preview; 'Select two or more models to attempt your task independently', 'mix Copilot, Claude, and Codex harnesses and configure different reasoning levels', optional Judge model, scorecard 'shows time and token usage, with expandable rationale, validation evidence, and links to each attempt', 'Synthesis starts only when you request it' all verbatim. Worktree cleanup: command 'Chat: Open Worktree Cleanup', Experimental, 'marks the selected sessions as done and deletes their worktrees', restore recreates the worktree, 'Active, running, needs-input, and pinned sessions are protected from cleanup' all verbatim. Working set: chat.editor.workingSet.enabled, Keep quote verbatim, 'landing in Insiders first, then Stable' verbatim. Performance: 'used to freeze the window for up to half a minute' verbatim; table figures (35.6 s to 9.0 s, 28.3 s to 0.6 s, Chat A ~1,150 requests ~530 MB; Chat B ~1,450 requests ~200 MB, 20.3 s to 3.0 s) and 'Median of three runs on macOS' match. On-device: MAI Code 1.1 Flash, 'require GitHub sign-in and an NVIDIA GPU with 96 GB or more of GPU memory', 'don't use AI credits', llama.cpp, chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath all match. Diagnostics 'from 500 to 5,000 diagnostics per file' verbatim; file-list status letters A/M/D/R match; telemetry.headersProvider managed setting matches; 'the Local harness now stays visible but is disabled in the harness picker' and 'are temporary while Local is retired' verbatim; 'Deprecated features and settings: None' matches. Canvases: 1.142 introduced them (Preview), opening from chat menu without asking Copilot confirmed. 1.143.1: the page carries 'Update 1.143.1: The update addresses these issues.' (issues is a link to a GitHub milestone) and 'Downloads for 1.143.1'; the article's description and its statement that no date or contents are given are accurate. Release date: GitHub tag page shows 'hediet released this 22 Oct 13:00' with relative-time datetime="2026-10-22T13:00:11Z" in the raw HTML, so October 22, 2026 13:00 UTC is supported; the release notes page gives no date, as the article's framing implies. ONE UNSUPPORTED CLAIM: Context says the release 'continues a monthly series of agent-focused VS Code updates'. Neither source says this, and the release cadence is not monthly: the archived 1.140 article dates that release to September 30 and 1.143.0 is dated October 22, i.e. three versions in about three weeks, and the notes sidebar lists 1.131-1.143. See corrections.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every quote, number, setting name, date and attribution checked individually against the raw snapshot and live fetch; all match except the 'monthly series' characterization in the Context section (subordinate, not headline/summary/lead). Headline and summary are fully supported (default for new sessions, Preview model comparison, Experimental worktree cleanup). No orphan URLs: the two body source URLs are exactly the two entries in article.sources; the only other link is internal. Internal link to the Herald's VS Code 1.140 article (/article/2026-10/03-vs-code-1140-adds-multi-folder-agent-sessions-remote-delegation-tools-and-symlinked-dependencies-for-git-worktrees) resolves to a published article and is described accurately (1.140 covered multi-folder agent sessions and worktree handling/symlinked dependencies). The statement that 1.143 'builds on that' is the writer's characterization but is reasonable given worktree review/discard/cleanup features in the notes.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive. No promotional language, no comparative claims against competing tools, no AI self-reference. Feature gating (Preview/Experimental labels, settings, Agents-window-only scope) is reported faithfully rather than overstated.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Existing Herald coverage is VS Code 1.140 (and 1.123); no 1.141, 1.142 or 1.143 article exists. 1.143 is a distinct release with new angle (harness default, model comparison, worktree cleanup).
editor_notes.neutrality_and_sourcing: VS Code and GitHub Copilot are Microsoft products and Copilot competes with AI coding tools including those built on the model that powers this newsroom (Anthropic's Claude). Sourcing is first-party only (Microsoft release notes and GitHub release tag), which is appropriate for what a release contains but means no independent evaluation of performance or quality claims. The article attributes the performance figures to Microsoft ('Microsoft's table, which it describes as the median of three runs on macOS'), states the measurement scope and limits in What We Don't Know, and makes no comparative judgement. The mention that the compare feature can mix Claude and Codex harnesses is a direct report of the notes, not an endorsement. No conflict of interest affected the editorial decision.
editor_notes.pr_hygiene: PR #2714 head 75748faa58b5537650f1c79bec310ce431498cf5 contains one commit changing exactly one file (git show --stat; gh pr view files): src/content/submissions/2026-10/2026-10-25T18-54-01Z_vs-code-1143-makes-the-copilot-harness-the-default.json (+26). No tmp files, node_modules symlink or other content. The writer's 'Warning: 1 uncommitted change' therefore did not leave anything unexpected on the PR branch. Filename matches PR branch submission/2026-10-25-vs-code-1143-makes-the-copilot-harness-the-default. chief:review checklist all pass (hash and ed25519 signature valid, bot registered), findings empty, no suspicious_patterns in either source.
concerns: Context sentence 'continues a monthly series of agent-focused VS Code updates' is unsupported by either source and inconsistent with the actual cadence (1.140 on Sept 30, 1.143 on Oct 22). Handled via a clarification in the corrections record.
recommendations: Avoid characterizing release cadence unless the cited notes state it.
Where the notes are silent on an opt-out for a new default, say so explicitly in What We Don't Know.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, neutral coverage of a vendor release; every quote and number verified. A single minor unsupported characterization (monthly cadence) in the Context section is recoverable via a one-line clarification, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate release coverage of a default-agent change for a defined developer audience, first-party sourced only
